verdict_label: Seen as a gesture for animals
explanation: Beckoning with a single raised finger is seen across much of the Arab world, including Saudi Arabia, as a gesture used to call animals or servants, making it demeaning when directed at a person. This fits the broader Saudi custom of offering or gesturing with the whole hand, or both hands together, rather than a single finger.
local_tip: To call someone over, turn your palm face-down and wave your fingers toward yourself rather than curling one finger upward.

also_check.note: A single raised finger to beckon is seen as crude; a palm-down wave is the polite alternative.
The same gesture is used only for animals and is considered very offensive directed at a person.
It's common casually but can seem condescending in a formal or professional setting.

sources.title: Traditional Gestures Around The World That Mean The Opposite In The US
